title: add-vpc-control-plane-terraform-route53-peering-sgs-endpoints-multi-az
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Add a first-class Terraform module to provision the VPC control plane networking required for Private deployments. This includes multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints (S3, KMS, ECR), security groups tuned for control-plane components, cross-account VPC peering support, and Route53 delegation/peering for private DNS zones. The goal is to let the Private installer and cloud onboarding scripts provision control-plane networking declaratively and reproducibly.

Summary of changes: - New module terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane that creates subnets (public/private) across AZs, NAT gateways, route tables, interface endpoints and gateway endpoints where applicable. - Security groups with least-privilege ingress for control-plane ports (6443-ish, health checks, metrics). - Optional cross-account VPC peering and automated route propagation when enabled. - Route53 private hosted zone delegation + zone-association resources and optional Route53 resolver rules for cross-account name resolution. - Outputs to feed the private-control-plane Helm chart and installer (vpc_id, subnet_ids, endpoint_ids, peering_connection_id, route53_zone_id). - Terratest-based integration tests and CI job added. - Docs: docs/vpc-control-plane.md with examples and migration notes.

Implementation notes: - Module is split into three logical files (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf) with minimal inline logic; heavy-lifting is done with data sources and modularized route table attachments. - Defaults are conservative: peering and Route53 delegation are opt-in boolean flags. - We avoid replacing existing route tables where possible; we create dedicated route tables for control-plane subnets and attach them to the provided subnet ids or newly created subnets. - KMS alias/resource looks up the provided key id if present, otherwise module leaves KMS integration disabled.

Testing and CI: - terraform fmt, tflint, and validate run on all changes. - Terratest suite boots a small control-plane VPC in our staging account, verifies endpoint reachability, peering route propagation, and DNS resolution across peered VPCs. - Initial CI run had one flaky terratest failure (DNS propagation timing); fixed by adding an explicit wait and idempotent retry in tests. All checks pass on final run.

Backward compatibility & migration: - Module is non-breaking by default; if consumers pass existing subnet ids we don't modify them. - For customers relying on an older, hand-rolled control plane network, migration guidance is provided in docs/vpc-control-plane.md (export current resources, pass IDs into module, enable optional features gradually).

Rollout plan: - Land module behind a feature flag in the installer for one release. - Use on staging environments and a single enterprise customer pilot. - After 2 weeks of monitoring and a successful pilot, flip defaults to the new module for new Private installs.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module with variables/outputs and examples
- [x] Terratest integration and CI job
- [x] Documentation and configuration examples
- [x] Security review for SGs (approver: Priya)
- [x] Operational runbook update

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the cross-account peering flow (variables: enable_peering / peering_owner_id) and the Route53 resolver/association permissions required. The tests include a mocked cross-account scenario using our staging "peered" accounts.
